th: Dùng cho hành động **đã kết thúc tại thời điểm xác định** trong quá khứ: yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago.
Use it for actions **finished at a definite time** in the past: yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago.

Động từ có quy tắc: thêm **-ed** (worked); kết thúc e → +d (lived); phụ âm + y → ied (studied); gấp đôi phụ âm (stopped).
Phát âm -ed:
• **/t/** sau âm vô thanh: worked, watched, stopped
• **/ɪd/** sau t, d: wanted, needed
• **/d/** còn lại: played, lived

Regular verbs add **-ed** (worked); e → +d (lived); consonant + y → ied (studied); doubling (stopped).
-ed pronunciation:
• **/t/** after voiceless sounds: worked, watched, stopped
• **/ɪd/** after t, d: wanted, needed
• **/d/** elsewhere: played, lived
Bất quy tắc thường gặp: go → went, see → saw, have → had, buy → bought, eat → ate, take → took, make → made, come → came, get → got, do → did.
Common irregulars: go → went, see → saw, have → had, buy → bought, eat → ate, take → took, make → made, come → came, get → got, do → did.
Phủ định / câu hỏi: **didn't / Did + động từ nguyên mẫu**. I didn't go. Did you see it? (Sai: didn't went)
Negative / question: **didn't / Did + base verb**. I didn't go. Did you see it? (Wrong: didn't went)
ex: I ___ to Da Nang last summer.
We visited our grandparents two weeks ago
Chúng tôi đã thăm ông bà hai tuần trước.
I bought a new phone yesterday.

warm.s: Last Saturday we wanted to go to the beach, but it rained all day, so we stayed at home and watched films.
q: Thứ Bảy tuần trước họ đã làm gì?
What did they do last Saturday?
o: stayed at home and watched films
e: Họ “wanted” (muốn) đi biển, nhưng vì mưa nên “stayed at home and watched films”. Đừng chọn theo ý định ban đầu.
They “wanted” to go to the beach, but because of the rain they “stayed at home and watched films”.
f: stayed at home and watched films

warm.s: I didn't go to school yesterday because I had a terrible headache and a high temperature.
e: Sau “didn't” dùng nguyên mẫu “go”; “had” là quá khứ bất quy tắc của “have”.
After “didn't” use the base form “go”; “had” is the irregular past of “have”.

warm.s: Two years ago, my family moved to a new flat, and I started at a new school.
e: Đuôi -ed: “moved” đọc /d/, “started” đọc /ɪd/ vì động từ tận cùng bằng âm /t/.
-ed endings: “moved” ends in /d/; “started” ends in /ɪd/ because the verb ends in /t/.

rd2.tx: Dear diary, yesterday was a very strange day. I woke up late because my alarm didn't ring, so I missed the bus and walked to work in the rain. When I arrived, my boss wasn't angry; she smiled and gave me a cup of hot coffee. At lunchtime, I went to a new restaurant with my colleagues, but the food was cold and expensive. In the evening, I found my old wallet under the sofa. I lost it three months ago! There was still 200,000 dong inside, so I bought a big cake for my family.
rd2.tr: Nhật ký thân mến, hôm qua là một ngày rất lạ. Tôi dậy muộn vì đồng hồ báo thức không kêu, nên tôi lỡ xe buýt và phải đi bộ đến chỗ làm dưới mưa. Khi tôi đến, sếp không hề giận; chị ấy mỉm cười và đưa cho tôi một tách cà phê nóng. Buổi trưa, tôi đi ăn ở một nhà hàng mới với đồng nghiệp, nhưng đồ ăn thì nguội và đắt. Buổi tối, tôi tìm thấy cái ví cũ dưới gầm ghế sofa. Tôi làm mất nó từ ba tháng trước! Bên trong vẫn còn 200.000 đồng, nên tôi mua một chiếc bánh kem to cho cả nhà.

q: Vì sao người viết dậy muộn?
Why did the writer wake up late?
o: Đồng hồ báo thức không kêu
e: “I woke up late because my alarm didn't ring” – lý do nằm ngay sau “because”.
“I woke up late because my alarm didn't ring” – the reason follows “because”.

q: Sếp đã phản ứng thế nào?
How did the boss react?
o: Mỉm cười và đưa cà phê
She smiled and gave her a coffee
e: “my boss wasn't angry; she smiled and gave me a cup of hot coffee”. Chú ý “wasn't angry” là phủ định – đừng chọn đáp án “rất giận”.
“my boss wasn't angry; she smiled and gave me a cup of hot coffee”. Watch the negative “wasn't”.
f: she smiled and gave me a cup of hot coffee

q: Người viết làm mất ví khi nào?
When did the writer lose the wallet?
e: “I lost it three months ago!” Hôm qua là lúc tìm thấy ví, không phải lúc làm mất.
“I lost it three months ago!” Yesterday is when she found it, not when she lost it.
f: I lost it three months ago

ex2.s: We ___ the museum last Sunday because it was closed for repairs, so we went to the park instead.
e: Phủ định quá khứ: “didn't + động từ nguyên mẫu”. “didn't visited” sai vì đã có quá khứ ở “did”; “not visited” thiếu trợ động từ.
Past negative: “didn't + base verb”. “didn't visited” doubles the past; “not visited” has no auxiliary.

ex2.s: My cousin ___ a second-hand motorbike two weeks ago, and now he rides it to university every day. (buy)
a: bought
e: “two weeks ago” → quá khứ đơn. “buy” là động từ bất quy tắc: buy → bought (không phải “buyed”).
“two weeks ago” → past simple. “buy” is irregular: buy → bought (not “buyed”).

ex2.s: Did you went to the concert in the park last night, or did you stay at home?
a: Did you go to the concert in the park last night, or did you stay at home?
Did you go to the concert in the park last night or did you stay at home?
e: Trong câu hỏi, “Did” đã mang thì quá khứ nên động từ chính về nguyên mẫu: “Did you go”, không phải “Did you went”.
In questions “Did” already shows the past, so the main verb is the base form: “Did you go”.

ex2.s: Tuần trước tôi tình cờ gặp một người bạn cũ ở siêu thị, và chúng tôi nói chuyện gần một tiếng.
a: Last week I met an old friend at the supermarket by chance, and we talked for almost an hour.
Last week I ran into an old friend at the supermarket, and we talked for almost an hour.
Last week I bumped into an old friend at the supermarket, and we talked for almost an hour.
Last week I met an old friend by chance at the supermarket, and we talked for nearly an hour.
Last week I ran into an old friend at the supermarket, and we talked for nearly an hour.
I met an old friend at the supermarket by chance last week, and we talked for almost an hour.
e: “Last week” → quá khứ đơn: meet → met (bất quy tắc), talk → talked. “tình cờ gặp” = meet by chance / run into / bump into. “gần một tiếng” = almost/nearly an hour (an vì h câm).
“Last week” → past simple: met, talked. “run into / bump into” = meet by chance. “an hour” because the h is silent.

q: Viết lại câu ở thể phủ định
Rewrite the sentence in the negative
ex2.s: I understood the teacher's explanation about the past simple in yesterday's lesson.
a: I didn't understand the teacher's explanation about the past simple in yesterday's lesson.
I did not understand the teacher's explanation about the past simple in yesterday's lesson.
e: Phủ định: “didn't + understand” (nguyên mẫu). Không viết “didn't understood”.
Negative: “didn't + understand” (base form). Not “didn't understood”.

ex2.s: Two days ago|my sister|lost her keys|on the way home,|so she|waited outside|until my mother|came back
m: Hai ngày trước chị tôi làm mất chìa khóa trên đường về, nên chị ấy phải đợi bên ngoài cho đến khi mẹ tôi về.
Two days ago my sister lost her keys on the way home, so she waited outside until my mother came back.
e: Cả ba động từ đều ở quá khứ đơn: lost (bất quy tắc), waited (/ɪd/), came (bất quy tắc). “until” nối hai hành động theo thứ tự thời gian.
All three verbs are past simple: lost (irregular), waited (/ɪd/), came (irregular). “until” links the two actions in time.

t: So sánh hơn & so sánh nhất
th:
Tính từ ngắn (1 âm tiết, hoặc 2 âm tiết tận cùng -y): **-er / the -est**.
• tall → taller → the tallest
• big → bigger → the biggest (gấp đôi phụ âm)
• happy → happier → the happiest

Short adjectives (1 syllable, or 2 ending in -y): **-er / the -est**.
• tall → taller → the tallest
• big → bigger → the biggest (double consonant)
• happy → happier → the happiest
Tính từ dài (2+ âm tiết): **more / the most**: more expensive, the most beautiful.
Long adjectives (2+ syllables): **more / the most**: more expensive, the most beautiful.
Bất quy tắc: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst; far → further → the furthest.
Irregular: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst; far → further → the furthest.
So sánh bằng: **as + tính từ + as** (She is as tall as me). Không bằng: **not as … as** (Hanoi is not as hot as Saigon).
Equality: **as + adjective + as** (She is as tall as me). Not equal: **not as … as** (Hanoi is not as hot as Saigon).
ex: This is ___ book I have ever read.
A car is ___ than a bike.
She is as tall than me.
She is as tall as me.
She is as taller as me.
Hanoi is not as hot as Saigon
Hà Nội không nóng bằng Sài Gòn.

warm.s: The train to Hue is slower than the plane, but it is much cheaper and more comfortable.
q: Điều gì đúng về tàu hỏa?
What is true about the train?
o: rẻ hơn và thoải mái hơn
e: Tàu “slower” (chậm hơn) nhưng “much cheaper and more comfortable”. “comfortable” dài nên dùng “more”.
The train is “slower” but “much cheaper and more comfortable”. “comfortable” is long, so it takes “more”.

warm.s: My new flat is bigger than my old one, but it is further from the city centre.
e: big → bigger (gấp đôi g). far → further (bất quy tắc); “farther” cũng đúng khi nói về khoảng cách.
big → bigger (double g). far → further (irregular); “farther” is also correct for distance.

warm.s: In my opinion, Hoi An is the most beautiful town in Vietnam, especially at night.
e: Nhấn “most” và “beautiful”; “the” trước “most” đọc nhẹ /ðə/.
Stress “most” and “beautiful”; say “the” weakly as /ðə/.

rd2.tx: Choosing a phone? We tested three popular models for students. The Alpha is the cheapest, at only three million dong, but its camera is the worst of the three. The Beta costs five million. Its battery is bigger than the Alpha's, so it lasts longer, and its screen is clearer. The Gamma is the most expensive phone, at nine million, and it has the best camera. However, it is also the heaviest, and it is not as fast as the Beta. For most students, we think the Beta is the best choice because it is good value for money.
rd2.tr: Bạn đang chọn điện thoại? Chúng tôi đã thử ba mẫu phổ biến dành cho sinh viên. Alpha rẻ nhất, chỉ ba triệu đồng, nhưng camera của nó tệ nhất trong ba chiếc. Beta có giá năm triệu. Pin của nó lớn hơn pin của Alpha nên dùng được lâu hơn, và màn hình cũng rõ hơn. Gamma là chiếc đắt nhất, chín triệu, và có camera tốt nhất. Tuy nhiên, nó cũng nặng nhất và không nhanh bằng Beta. Với phần lớn sinh viên, chúng tôi nghĩ Beta là lựa chọn tốt nhất vì đáng đồng tiền.

q: Điện thoại nào rẻ nhất?
Which phone is the cheapest?
e: “The Alpha is the cheapest, at only three million dong.”
“The Alpha is the cheapest, at only three million dong.”

q: Vì sao pin của Beta dùng lâu hơn Alpha?
Why does the Beta's battery last longer than the Alpha's?
e: “Its battery is bigger than the Alpha's, so it lasts longer” – “so” nối nguyên nhân với kết quả.
“Its battery is bigger than the Alpha's, so it lasts longer” – “so” links cause and result.
f: Its battery is bigger than the Alpha's

q: Câu nào ĐÚNG về Gamma?
Which is TRUE about the Gamma?
o: It is faster than the Beta.
e: “it is also the heaviest”. Bài nói Gamma “not as fast as the Beta” (không nhanh bằng), và camera của nó tốt nhất.
“it is also the heaviest”. It is “not as fast as the Beta”, and it has the best camera.

ex2.s: This winter is ___ than last winter, so I bought a thicker coat and a warm scarf.
e: “cold” là tính từ một âm tiết → thêm -er: colder. Có “than” nên không dùng so sánh nhất “the coldest”.
“cold” has one syllable → “colder”. “than” means a comparative, not “the coldest”.

ex2.s: Hung is the ___ student in my class, so the teacher often asks him to help the others. (good)
a: best
e: “good” bất quy tắc: good → better → the best. Có “the” và “in my class” nên cần so sánh nhất.
“good” is irregular: good → better → the best. “the … in my class” needs the superlative.

ex2.s: My brother is more tall than my father now, although he is only fifteen years old.
a: My brother is taller than my father now, although he is only fifteen years old.
My brother is taller than my father now, although he's only fifteen years old.
e: “tall” là tính từ ngắn nên dùng “taller”, không dùng “more tall”. “more” chỉ dùng cho tính từ dài như “more expensive”.
“tall” is short, so use “taller”, not “more tall”. “more” is for long adjectives like “more expensive”.

ex2.s: Hà Nội không đông bằng Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, nhưng mùa đông ở đây lạnh hơn nhiều.
a: Hanoi is not as crowded as Ho Chi Minh City, but the winter here is much colder.
Hanoi isn't as crowded as Ho Chi Minh City, but the winter here is much colder.
Hanoi is not as crowded as Ho Chi Minh City, but winter here is much colder.
Hanoi isn't as crowded as Ho Chi Minh City, but winter here is much colder.
Hanoi is not as crowded as Ho Chi Minh City, but winters here are much colder.
Hanoi isn't as crowded as Ho Chi Minh City, but winters here are much colder.
Hanoi is less crowded than Ho Chi Minh City, but the winter here is much colder.
e: “không … bằng” = “not as + tính từ + as”. “lạnh hơn nhiều” = “much colder” (không nói “very colder”).
“not as … as” for “not equal”. To make a comparative stronger, use “much colder”, never “very colder”.

q: Viết lại phần đầu câu với “not as … as” (dùng “fast”) mà nghĩa không đổi
Rewrite the first part with “not as … as” (use “fast”) keeping the meaning
ex2.s: Bicycles are slower than motorbikes, but they are much better for the environment.
a: Bicycles are not as fast as motorbikes, but they are much better for the environment.
Bicycles aren't as fast as motorbikes, but they are much better for the environment.
Bicycles aren't as fast as motorbikes, but they're much better for the environment.
e: “slower than” = “not as fast as”. Sau “as” dùng tính từ nguyên dạng “fast”, không dùng “faster”.
“slower than” = “not as fast as”. Use the plain adjective “fast” between the two “as”.

ex2.s: This is|the most delicious|bowl of pho|I have ever eaten,|and it is|cheaper than|the one near my house
m: Đây là bát phở ngon nhất mà tôi từng ăn, và nó còn rẻ hơn bát phở gần nhà tôi.
This is the most delicious bowl of pho I have ever eaten, and it is cheaper than the one near my house.
e: “delicious” dài → “the most delicious”. “cheap” ngắn → “cheaper than”. “the one” thay cho “the bowl of pho”.
“delicious” is long → “the most delicious”; “cheap” is short → “cheaper than”. “the one” replaces “the bowl of pho”.

t: Tương lai: will & be going to
th: **will + V**: quyết định ngay lúc nói (The phone's ringing – I'll get it!), dự đoán theo ý kiến (I think it will rain), lời hứa, đề nghị (I'll help you).
**will + V**: instant decisions (The phone's ringing – I'll get it!), opinion-based predictions (I think it will rain), promises and offers (I'll help you).
**be going to + V**: kế hoạch đã định trước (I'm going to visit Japan next month) và dự đoán có bằng chứng (Look at those clouds – it's going to rain).
**be going to + V**: plans made before (I'm going to visit Japan next month) and predictions with evidence (Look at those clouds – it's going to rain).
Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho lịch hẹn đã sắp xếp: I'm meeting Tom at 7 tonight.
Present continuous for fixed arrangements: I'm meeting Tom at 7 tonight.
vo: to say you will surely do something
grey or white mass in the sky
ex: The phone is ringing. You say?
Quyết định ngay lúc nói → will.
Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain.
Có bằng chứng trước mắt → going to.
We ___ visit Hue next month. We've bought the tickets.
I promise I ___ call you tonight.
Viết dạng rút gọn của “I will”
I think Vietnam ___ win the match.
Are you going to study tonight
Tối nay bạn có định học không?
I will help you with your homework.

warm.s: My parents are going to visit Ha Long Bay next month, and they booked the boat trip last week.
q: Tháng sau bố mẹ sẽ làm gì?
What are the parents doing next month?
e: “are going to visit” = kế hoạch đã định; bằng chứng là họ đã đặt tour tuần trước (“booked … last week”).
“are going to visit” is a fixed plan; they already “booked the boat trip last week”.

warm.s: Don't worry about the heavy bags, because I will carry them to the car for you.
e: “I will carry” là lời đề nghị giúp đỡ quyết định ngay lúc nói. Có thể nghe thành “I'll carry”.
“I will carry” is an offer made at the moment of speaking. You may hear the contraction “I'll”.

warm.s: Look at those black clouds over the mountains; I think it's going to rain very soon.
e: “going to” trong văn nói thường đọc nhanh /ˈɡəʊ.ɪŋ tə/; nhấn “black”, “clouds”, “rain”.
“going to” is said quickly /ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə/; stress “black”, “clouds”, “rain”.

rd2.tx: Hi Ben, thanks for your message! Yes, I'm free this summer. I'm going to spend two weeks with my grandparents in Nha Trang in July, because they're having a big party for my grandfather's eightieth birthday. After that, I'm going to start a part-time job at a bookshop. I'm not sure about August yet, but maybe I'll take a short English course. When are you coming to Vietnam? If you come in August, I'll show you around Hanoi, and I promise I won't take you to boring museums! Write back soon. Minh
rd2.tr: Chào Ben, cảm ơn tin nhắn của cậu! Ừ, hè này mình rảnh. Tháng Bảy mình định ở với ông bà ở Nha Trang hai tuần, vì ông bà sẽ tổ chức một bữa tiệc lớn mừng sinh nhật lần thứ tám mươi của ông. Sau đó mình sẽ bắt đầu làm thêm ở một hiệu sách. Tháng Tám thì mình chưa chắc, nhưng có lẽ mình sẽ học một khóa tiếng Anh ngắn. Khi nào cậu sang Việt Nam? Nếu cậu sang vào tháng Tám, mình sẽ dẫn cậu đi thăm Hà Nội, và mình hứa sẽ không đưa cậu đến mấy bảo tàng chán ngắt đâu! Nhớ trả lời sớm nhé. Minh

q: Minh sẽ ở Nha Trang bao lâu?
How long will Minh stay in Nha Trang?
e: “I'm going to spend two weeks with my grandparents in Nha Trang” – kế hoạch đã định.
“I'm going to spend two weeks with my grandparents” – a fixed plan.
f: I'm going to spend two weeks

q: Kế hoạch nào Minh CHƯA chắc chắn?
Which plan is Minh NOT sure about?
e: “I'm not sure… but maybe I'll take a short English course”. “maybe + will” cho thấy chưa chắc; hai kế hoạch kia dùng “going to” vì đã quyết định.
“maybe I'll take…” shows uncertainty; the other two plans use “going to” because they are decided.
f: maybe I'll take a short English course

q: Minh hứa điều gì với Ben?
What does Minh promise Ben?
o: sẽ dẫn Ben đi bảo tàng
sẽ không dẫn Ben đến bảo tàng nhàm chán
not to take Ben to boring museums
sẽ đón Ben ở sân bay
to meet Ben at the airport
e: “I promise I won't take you to boring museums” – lời hứa dùng “will / won't”. “won't” = will not.
“I promise I won't take you to boring museums” – promises use will/won't. “won't” = will not.
f: I promise I won't take you

ex2.s: My sister saved money all year, and she ___ buy a new laptop when the sale starts next month.
e: Cô ấy đã để dành tiền cả năm → kế hoạch có sẵn → “is going to”. “will to” sai cấu trúc; “going to” thiếu “is”.
She saved all year, so it's a plan → “is going to”. “will to” is wrong; “going to” is missing “is”.

ex2.s: It's very hot in here, isn't it? Wait a moment, and I ___ open the window for you.
a: will
e: Quyết định / đề nghị ngay lúc nói → “will”. Không dùng “am going to” vì trước đó chưa có kế hoạch.
An instant decision or offer → “will”. Not “am going to”, because there was no plan before.

ex2.s: I think our team wins the match on Saturday because our best player is back from injury.
a: I think our team will win the match on Saturday because our best player is back from injury.
I think our team'll win the match on Saturday because our best player is back from injury.
e: Dự đoán theo ý kiến cá nhân (I think…) về tương lai → “will win”, không dùng hiện tại đơn “wins”.
An opinion-based prediction (I think…) about the future → “will win”, not the present “wins”.

ex2.s: Tôi định học tiếng Tây Ban Nha vào năm sau vì tôi muốn đi du lịch Nam Mỹ.
a: I am going to study Spanish next year because I want to travel to South America.
I'm going to study Spanish next year because I want to travel to South America.
I'm going to learn Spanish next year because I want to travel to South America.
I am going to learn Spanish next year because I want to travel to South America.
Next year I'm going to learn Spanish because I want to travel to South America.
Next year I am going to study Spanish because I want to travel to South America.
I'm going to learn Spanish next year because I want to travel around South America.
e: “định” = kế hoạch đã có từ trước → “be going to”. Sau “want” cần “to + động từ”: want to travel.
“định” means a plan → “be going to”. After “want” use “to + verb”: want to travel.

q: Viết lại câu dùng “be going to” vì có dấu hiệu ngay trước mắt
Rewrite with “be going to” because there is clear evidence
ex2.s: Be careful! The glass is at the edge of the table, and it will fall.
a: Be careful! The glass is at the edge of the table, and it is going to fall.
Be careful! The glass is at the edge of the table, and it's going to fall.
e: Cái cốc đang ở mép bàn = bằng chứng nhìn thấy được → “is going to fall”. “will” dùng cho dự đoán theo ý kiến, không có bằng chứng.
The glass at the edge is visible evidence → “is going to fall”. “will” is for opinion-based predictions.

ex2.s: I'm meeting|my old classmates|at a restaurant|in the city centre|at seven o'clock|tomorrow evening
m: Tối mai lúc bảy giờ tôi có hẹn gặp các bạn học cũ ở một nhà hàng trung tâm thành phố.
I'm meeting my old classmates at a restaurant in the city centre at seven o'clock tomorrow evening.
e: Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho cuộc hẹn đã sắp xếp (có giờ, có địa điểm). Thứ tự: nơi chốn trước, thời gian sau.
Present continuous for a fixed arrangement. Order: place first, then time.

t: Danh từ đếm được & không đếm được
th: Đếm được: có số nhiều (apples, books). Không đếm được: **water, rice, money, information, advice, furniture, news** – không có số nhiều, không dùng a/an.
Countable: have plurals (apples, books). Uncountable: **water, rice, money, information, advice, furniture, news** – no plural, no a/an.
**some**: câu khẳng định và lời mời/đề nghị (Would you like some tea?). **any**: câu phủ định và câu hỏi.
**some**: positive sentences and offers (Would you like some tea?). **any**: negatives and questions.
**many** + danh từ đếm được số nhiều; **much** + không đếm được (chủ yếu phủ định/câu hỏi); **a lot of** dùng cho cả hai. How many…? / How much…?
**many** + plural countable; **much** + uncountable (mostly negatives/questions); **a lot of** for both. How many…? / How much…?
**a few** (đếm được) / **a little** (không đếm được) = một vài, một chút (ý tích cực). **few / little** = rất ít (ý tiêu cực).
**a few** (countable) / **a little** (uncountable) = some (positive). **few / little** = almost none (negative).
vo: an opinion about what to do

There is ___ information on the website.
How many people are coming to the party
Bao nhiêu người sẽ đến bữa tiệc?

warm.s: We don't need any rice this week, but we need a little sugar and a few eggs for the cake.
q: Họ cần mua gì?
What do they need?
e: “don't need any rice” = không cần gạo; “need a little sugar and a few eggs”. “a little” cho danh từ không đếm được, “a few” cho đếm được.
They don't need rice; they need “a little sugar” (uncountable) and “a few eggs” (countable).
f: a little sugar and a few eggs

warm.s: How much money do you usually spend on food and transport every month in the city?
e: “money” không đếm được → “How much”. “spend money on something” = tiêu tiền vào việc gì.
“money” is uncountable → “How much”. “spend money on something”.

warm.s: My teacher gave me some useful advice about how to learn new words every day.
e: “advice” (danh từ) đọc /ədˈvaɪs/ với âm /s/; khác với động từ “advise” /ədˈvaɪz/.
The noun “advice” ends in /s/; the verb “advise” ends in /z/.

rd2.tx: Hi Tom, I'm at work until seven, so can you go to the supermarket for me? We're having a small party tomorrow and we don't have much food in the house. Please buy some rice, a few onions and a bottle of fish sauce. We have a lot of eggs, so don't buy any. How many people are coming? I think about ten, so we need a lot of fruit too, maybe some mangoes and a big watermelon. There is a little money in the drawer next to the fridge. Thanks! Lan
rd2.tr: Chào Tom, mình làm đến bảy giờ, nên cậu đi siêu thị giúp mình được không? Mai nhà mình có một bữa tiệc nhỏ mà trong nhà không còn nhiều đồ ăn. Cậu mua giúp ít gạo, vài củ hành và một chai nước mắm nhé. Nhà còn nhiều trứng lắm, nên đừng mua. Có bao nhiêu người đến nhỉ? Mình nghĩ khoảng mười người, nên mình cũng cần nhiều hoa quả, có thể là ít xoài và một quả dưa hấu to. Có một ít tiền trong ngăn kéo cạnh tủ lạnh. Cảm ơn nhé! Lan

q: Vì sao Lan nhờ Tom đi siêu thị?
Why does Lan ask Tom to go shopping?
o: vì cô ấy làm việc đến bảy giờ
because she is at work until seven
vì Tom thích đi mua sắm
e: “I'm at work until seven, so can you go…” – “so” cho thấy đây là lý do.
“I'm at work until seven, so…” – “so” shows this is the reason.

q: Tom KHÔNG nên mua gì?
What should Tom NOT buy?
e: “We have a lot of eggs, so don't buy any.” “any” dùng trong câu phủ định.
“We have a lot of eggs, so don't buy any.” “any” is used in negatives.
f: We have a lot of eggs, so don't buy any

q: Tiền để ở đâu?
Where is the money?
o: trong ngăn kéo cạnh tủ lạnh
in the drawer next to the fridge
e: “There is a little money in the drawer next to the fridge.” Chú ý “There is” (không phải “are”) vì “money” không đếm được.
“There is a little money in the drawer next to the fridge.” Note “is”, because “money” is uncountable.
f: in the drawer next to the fridge

ex2.s: I can't give you ___ information about the trip now, but I will send you an email tonight.
e: “information” không đếm được → “much” trong câu phủ định. “many” và “a few” chỉ đi với danh từ đếm được số nhiều.
“information” is uncountable → “much” in a negative. “many” and “a few” need plural countable nouns.

ex2.s: How ___ people came to your birthday party last weekend, and did they bring any presents?
a: many
e: “people” là danh từ đếm được số nhiều (số nhiều của “person”) → “How many”.
“people” is a plural countable noun (plural of “person”) → “How many”.

ex2.s: My grandmother gave me some good advices before I left home to study in Hanoi.
a: My grandmother gave me some good advice before I left home to study in Hanoi.
My grandmother gave me some good pieces of advice before I left home to study in Hanoi.
e: “advice” không đếm được nên không có dạng “advices”. Muốn đếm, dùng “a piece of advice / pieces of advice”.
“advice” is uncountable, so there is no “advices”. To count it, say “a piece / pieces of advice”.

ex2.s: Chúng ta còn rất ít thời gian, nên hãy bắt taxi thay vì đi xe buýt.
a: We have very little time, so let's take a taxi instead of the bus.
We have very little time left, so let's take a taxi instead of the bus.
We have very little time, so let's take a taxi instead of taking the bus.
We have very little time left, so let's take a taxi instead of taking the bus.
We don't have much time, so let's take a taxi instead of the bus.
We don't have much time left, so let's take a taxi instead of taking the bus.
We have very little time left, so let's get a taxi instead of the bus.
e: “time” ở đây không đếm được → “little / very little” (rất ít, ý tiêu cực) hoặc “not much”. Không dùng “few time”.
“time” here is uncountable → “(very) little” or “not much”. Never “few time”.

q: Viết lại thành câu hỏi, bắt đầu bằng “Is there”
Rewrite as a question starting with “Is there”
ex2.s: There is some cheese left in the fridge for our sandwiches tomorrow morning.
a: Is there any cheese left in the fridge for our sandwiches tomorrow morning?
e: Trong câu hỏi thông thường, “some” đổi thành “any”. “cheese” không đếm được nên dùng “Is there”.
In ordinary questions “some” becomes “any”. “cheese” is uncountable, so “Is there”.

ex2.s: There isn't|much furniture|in my new flat|yet,|so I'm going to|buy a sofa|and a few chairs|next weekend
m: Căn hộ mới của tôi chưa có nhiều đồ nội thất, nên cuối tuần sau tôi sẽ mua một chiếc sofa và vài cái ghế.
There isn't much furniture in my new flat yet, so I'm going to buy a sofa and a few chairs next weekend.
e: “furniture” không đếm được → “isn't much”. “chairs” đếm được → “a few chairs”.
“furniture” is uncountable → “isn't much”. “chairs” are countable → “a few chairs”.

th:
**Đặt phòng và hỏi thông tin** – dùng câu lịch sự:
• **I'd like to book** a double room for three nights.
• **Do you have** a room with a sea view?
• **Is breakfast included?** / **How much is it** per night?
• **Could you** send me a confirmation email, please?
“I'd like” (= I would like) lịch sự hơn nhiều so với “I want”.

**Booking and asking for information** – use polite forms:
• **I'd like to book** a double room for three nights.
• **Do you have** a room with a sea view?
• **Is breakfast included?** / **How much is it** per night?
• **Could you** send me a confirmation email, please?
“I'd like” (= I would like) is much more polite than “I want”.

**Hỏi và chỉ đường**:
• Hỏi: **Excuse me, could you tell me the way to** the station? / **How do I get to**…?
• Chỉ: **go straight on**, **turn left / right**, **take the second turning on the left**, **it's on your right**, **it's opposite / next to**…
Ở sân bay: **check in** (làm thủ tục), **boarding pass** (thẻ lên máy bay), **gate** (cổng), **delayed** (bị hoãn), **luggage** (hành lý – không đếm được, không nói “luggages”).

**Asking for and giving directions**:
• Ask: **Excuse me, could you tell me the way to** the station? / **How do I get to**…?
• Give: **go straight on**, **turn left / right**, **take the second turning on the left**, **it's on your right**, **it's opposite / next to**…
At the airport: **check in**, **boarding pass**, **gate**, **delayed**, **luggage** (uncountable – never “luggages”).

**Phàn nàn lịch sự**: nêu vấn đề nhẹ nhàng rồi đưa ra yêu cầu cụ thể.
• **I'm afraid there's a problem with** my room.
• The air conditioning **doesn't work**. / There's **no hot water**.
• **Could you send someone to fix it?** / **Could I change rooms, please?**
Trong email phàn nàn, kể lại sự việc bằng **quá khứ đơn** và kết thúc bằng một yêu cầu rõ ràng (a refund, a discount).

**Complaining politely**: state the problem gently, then make a clear request.
• **I'm afraid there's a problem with** my room.
• The air conditioning **doesn't work**. / There's **no hot water**.
• **Could you send someone to fix it?** / **Could I change rooms, please?**
In a complaint email, tell the story in the **past simple** and finish with a clear request (a refund, a discount).

a hotel room for two people
làm thủ tục (khách sạn, sân bay)
to report your arrival at a hotel or airport
a card that lets you get on a plane
bags and cases you take on a trip

to say that something is wrong or not good enough

warm.s: Go straight along this street, take the second turning on the left, and the hotel is opposite the post office.
q: Khách sạn ở đâu?
Where is the hotel?
e: “the hotel is opposite the post office” – đối diện. Hãy nghe kỹ giới từ ở cuối câu chỉ đường.
“the hotel is opposite the post office”. Listen carefully for the preposition at the end of directions.

warm.s: Passengers on flight VN245 to Bangkok, please go to gate twelve now, because the flight is boarding.
q: Hành khách phải đi đến đâu?
Where must the passengers go?
e: “gate twelve” = cổng 12. “twelve” /twelv/ khác “twenty” /ˈtwen.ti/ ở âm cuối.
“gate twelve” = gate 12. “twelve” /twelv/ and “twenty” /ˈtwen.ti/ have different endings.

warm.s: I'd like to book a double room for three nights, from the fifth to the eighth of June.
e: “I'd like to book” = I would like to book (lịch sự). Ngày tháng dùng số thứ tự: the fifth, the eighth.
“I'd like to book” = I would like to book (polite). Dates use ordinals: the fifth, the eighth.

warm.s: Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the nearest bus stop, please?
e: “could you” thường nối thành /kʊ.dʒu/. Lên giọng nhẹ ở cuối câu hỏi lịch sự.
“could you” is often linked as /kʊ.dʒu/. Use a gentle rise at the end of a polite question.

rd2.tx: Dear Sir or Madam, I stayed at your hotel from 3rd to 6th May, and I would like to tell you about some problems. When I booked online, I asked for a quiet double room with a sea view. However, the receptionist gave me a small room next to the lift, with no view at all. On the second night, the air conditioning didn't work, so I couldn't sleep because it was too hot. I called reception twice, but nobody came to fix it. The breakfast was excellent and the staff were friendly, but I paid extra for a sea view. Could you please give me a partial refund? Yours faithfully, Lan Pham
rd2.tr: Kính gửi Quý khách sạn, tôi đã ở khách sạn của quý vị từ ngày 3 đến ngày 6 tháng Năm, và tôi muốn phản ánh một số vấn đề. Khi đặt phòng trực tuyến, tôi đã yêu cầu một phòng đôi yên tĩnh nhìn ra biển. Tuy nhiên, nhân viên lễ tân lại đưa cho tôi một phòng nhỏ cạnh thang máy, hoàn toàn không có tầm nhìn. Vào đêm thứ hai, điều hòa không hoạt động, nên tôi không ngủ được vì quá nóng. Tôi đã gọi lễ tân hai lần nhưng không ai đến sửa. Bữa sáng rất ngon và nhân viên thân thiện, nhưng tôi đã trả thêm tiền cho phòng nhìn ra biển. Quý vị có thể hoàn lại cho tôi một phần tiền được không? Trân trọng, Phạm Lan

q: Khi đặt phòng, Lan đã yêu cầu loại phòng nào?
What kind of room did Lan ask for when she booked?
o: a small room next to the lift
phòng đôi yên tĩnh nhìn ra biển
a quiet double room with a sea view
e: “I asked for a quiet double room with a sea view.” Phòng cạnh thang máy là phòng cô ấy NHẬN, không phải phòng cô ấy đặt.
“I asked for a quiet double room with a sea view.” The room next to the lift is what she GOT, not what she booked.
f: a quiet double room with a sea view

q: Chuyện gì xảy ra vào đêm thứ hai?
What happened on the second night?
e: “On the second night, the air conditioning didn't work” – vì vậy cô ấy không ngủ được.
“On the second night, the air conditioning didn't work” – so she couldn't sleep.

q: Lan muốn khách sạn làm gì?
What does Lan want the hotel to do?
o: đổi phòng cho cô ấy ngay
xin lỗi nhân viên lễ tân
e: Câu yêu cầu ở cuối thư: “Could you please give me a partial refund?” – “partial refund” = hoàn lại một phần tiền.
The request at the end: “Could you please give me a partial refund?” – part of the money back.

ex2.s: Excuse me, ___ you tell me how to get to the train station from here, please?
e: “Could you…?” là cách nhờ vả lịch sự. “should” là lời khuyên, “must” là bắt buộc – đều không hợp khi hỏi đường người lạ.
“Could you…?” is a polite request. “should” gives advice and “must” is an obligation – both sound wrong to a stranger.

ex2.s: Our flight to Singapore was ___ for three hours because of a storm, so we waited in the airport café.
a: delayed
e: “delayed” = bị hoãn, trễ giờ. Không dùng “cancelled” vì chuyến bay vẫn bay sau ba tiếng.
“delayed” means later than planned. Not “cancelled”, because the flight still left after three hours.

ex2.s: I would like to book a double room for two nights, and could you tell me if breakfast is include?
a: I would like to book a double room for two nights, and could you tell me if breakfast is included?
I'd like to book a double room for two nights, and could you tell me if breakfast is included?
e: Cụm cố định “Is breakfast included?” dùng dạng bị động “is included” (được bao gồm). Thiếu -d là lỗi rất hay gặp.
The fixed phrase is “Is breakfast included?” – passive “is included”. Missing the -d is a very common mistake.

ex2.s: Xin lỗi, tôi e là phòng của tôi có vấn đề: vòi sen không có nước nóng.
a: Excuse me, I'm afraid there is a problem with my room: there is no hot water in the shower.
Excuse me, I'm afraid there's a problem with my room: there's no hot water in the shower.
Excuse me, I'm afraid there is a problem with my room: the shower has no hot water.
Excuse me, I'm afraid there's a problem with my room: the shower doesn't have any hot water.
Excuse me, I'm afraid there is a problem with my room: there isn't any hot water in the shower.
Sorry, I'm afraid there is a problem with my room: there is no hot water in the shower.
e: “tôi e là” = “I'm afraid” – cách mở đầu phàn nàn lịch sự. “nước nóng” không đếm được nên dùng “no hot water” hoặc “isn't any hot water”.
“I'm afraid” softens a complaint. “hot water” is uncountable: “no hot water” or “isn't any hot water”.
f: I'm afraid there is a problem with my room

q: Viết lại thành lời đề nghị lịch sự, bắt đầu bằng “Could you”
Rewrite as a polite request starting with “Could you”
ex2.s: Give me a room on a higher floor because the street outside is too noisy at night.
a: Could you give me a room on a higher floor, please, because the street outside is too noisy at night?
Could you please give me a room on a higher floor because the street outside is too noisy at night?
Could you give me a room on a higher floor because the street outside is too noisy at night?
Could you give me a room on a higher floor because the street outside is too noisy at night, please?
e: Câu mệnh lệnh nghe khá thô với nhân viên khách sạn; “Could you + động từ nguyên mẫu…?” lịch sự hơn. Nhớ đổi dấu chấm thành dấu hỏi.
An imperative sounds rude to hotel staff; “Could you + base verb…?” is polite. Change the full stop to a question mark.

ex2.s: You need to|show your passport|and boarding pass|at the gate|before you|get on|the plane
m: Bạn cần xuất trình hộ chiếu và thẻ lên máy bay ở cổng trước khi lên máy bay.
You need to show your passport and boarding pass at the gate before you get on the plane.
e: “need to + động từ” = cần làm gì. “get on the plane” = lên máy bay (không dùng “get in” cho máy bay, tàu, xe buýt).
“need to + verb”. We “get on” a plane, train or bus, not “get in”.

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – danh từ đếm được / không đếm được:** đếm được có số nhiều (an egg, two eggs); không đếm được không có số nhiều (water, rice, sugar). **some** dùng trong câu khẳng định và lời mời/yêu cầu; **any** trong câu phủ định và câu hỏi; **many** + đếm được, **much** + không đếm được.
• Could I have some water, please?
• We haven't got any eggs.
• How much sugar do you want? – How many people are there?

**Grammar 1 – countable / uncountable nouns:** countable nouns have plurals (an egg, two eggs); uncountable nouns don't (water, rice, sugar). **some** in positive sentences, offers and requests; **any** in negatives and questions; **many** + countable, **much** + uncountable.
• Could I have some water, please?
• We haven't got any eggs.
• How much sugar do you want? – How many people are there?

**Ngữ pháp 2 – gọi món lịch sự:** **I'd like** (= I would like) + danh từ; **Could I have …, please?** Tránh nói “I want” với phục vụ vì nghe cộc.
• I'd like the chicken, please.
• Could we have the bill, please?

**Grammar 2 – ordering politely:** **I'd like** (= I would like) + noun; **Could I have …, please?** Avoid “I want” with waiters – it sounds rude.
• I'd like the chicken, please.
• Could we have the bill, please?
**Phát âm – dạng yếu /ə/:** trong câu nói nhanh, a, of, and đọc nhẹ thành /ə/, /əv/, /ən/: a cup of tea /ə ˈkʌp əv ˈtiː/, fish and chips /ˌfɪʃ ən ˈtʃɪps/. Chỉ nhấn vào từ chính (cup, tea).
**Pronunciation – weak form /ə/:** in fast speech a, of and and become /ə/, /əv/, /ən/: a cup of tea /ə ˈkʌp əv ˈtiː/, fish and chips /ˌfɪʃ ən ˈtʃɪps/. Only stress the key words (cup, tea).

**Tự luyện ngoài app:**
• Nghe (20 phút): nghe 1 hội thoại gọi món, ghi lại món, số lượng và giá.
• Nói (25 phút): đóng vai khách và phục vụ – đặt bàn, gọi 3 món, hỏi độ cay, tính tiền; ghi âm cả hai vai.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc một thực đơn thật, chọn bữa ăn dưới một mức giá cho trước.
• Viết (30 phút): viết đánh giá nhà hàng 80 từ: món, giá, phục vụ, có quay lại không.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): phân loại 20 món quen thuộc: thịt, rau, đồ uống, tráng miệng.
• Thử thách (20 phút): xem một video nấu ăn tiếng Anh, ghi 10 nguyên liệu và 5 động từ nấu (cut, fry, boil…).

**Practice outside the app:**
• Listening (20 min): listen to a restaurant ordering dialogue; note dishes, quantities and prices.
• Speaking (25 min): role-play customer and waiter – book a table, order 3 dishes, ask if it's spicy, pay; record both roles.
• Reading (20 min): read a real menu and choose a meal under a set budget.
• Writing (30 min): write an 80-word restaurant review: food, price, service, would you go back?
• Vocabulary (15 min): sort 20 familiar foods into meat, vegetables, drinks and desserts.
• Challenge (20 min): watch an English cooking video; note 10 ingredients and 5 cooking verbs (cut, fry, boil…).

Tôi không ăn được đồ cay.
Could I have another bottle of water?
Cho tôi thêm một chai nước.
vo: a list of dishes in a restaurant
ask for food in a restaurant
small white grains you cook and eat
the paper that shows how much to pay
a person who serves food in a restaurant

warm.s: We'd like a table for four, please, and could you bring us some water while we look at the menu?
q: Khách xin gì trong lúc xem thực đơn?
What do the customers ask for while they look at the menu?
e: “could you bring us some water while we look at the menu” – họ xin nước. “some” dùng trong lời yêu cầu dù là câu hỏi.
“could you bring us some water while we look at the menu” – they want water. “some” is used in requests even in questions.

warm.s: Could I see the menu, please?
e: Yêu cầu lịch sự: Could I + động từ nguyên mẫu. Nhớ dấu phẩy trước “please” và dấu hỏi.
Polite request: Could I + base verb. Remember the comma before “please” and the question mark.

warm.s: I'd like a bowl of pho.
e: “I'd” = I would. “a bowl of” đọc nhẹ /ə ˈboʊl əv/.
“I'd” = I would. Say “a bowl of” lightly: /ə ˈboʊl əv/.

warm.s: Could we have the bill, please?
e: “the bill” (Anh-Anh) = “the check” (Anh-Mỹ). Không viết “Could we have bill”.
“the bill” (British) = “the check” (American). Don't drop “the”.

warm.s: My favourite dish is bun cha because the grilled pork is delicious and the sauce is a little sweet.
e: Câu hỏi: What's your favourite dish? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Nhấn vào “favourite”, “delicious” /dɪˈlɪʃ.əs/ (trọng âm âm tiết 2).
Question: What's your favourite dish? – Model answer. Stress “favourite” and “delicious” /dɪˈlɪʃ.əs/ (stress on syllable 2).

warm.s: I prefer cooking at home because it's cheaper and healthier, but I sometimes eat out with friends at the weekend.
e: Câu hỏi: Do you prefer cooking at home or eating out? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. “prefer” nhấn âm tiết 2 /prɪˈfɝː/; “eat out” đọc nối /iːt̬ ˈaʊt/.
Question: Do you prefer cooking at home or eating out? – Model answer. “prefer” is stressed on syllable 2 /prɪˈfɝː/; link “eat out” /iːt̬ ˈaʊt/.

rd2.tx: Last Friday I went to Hoa Sen, a small Vietnamese restaurant near my office. I booked a table for two, so we didn't wait. The waiter was very friendly and he brought us the menu and some cold water. My friend ordered a bowl of beef pho and I had fried rice with chicken. I asked, “Is this dish spicy?” and the waiter said, “Only a little.” The food was delicious, but there wasn't much chicken in my rice. For dessert we shared a sweet mango cake. The bill was only twenty dollars. I'm going to go back next month with my family.
rd2.tr: Thứ Sáu tuần trước tôi đến Hoa Sen, một nhà hàng Việt nhỏ gần văn phòng tôi. Tôi đã đặt bàn cho hai người nên chúng tôi không phải chờ. Người phục vụ rất thân thiện, anh ấy mang cho chúng tôi thực đơn và một ít nước lạnh. Bạn tôi gọi một bát phở bò còn tôi ăn cơm rang gà. Tôi hỏi: “Món này có cay không?” và người phục vụ nói: “Chỉ hơi cay thôi.” Đồ ăn rất ngon, nhưng trong cơm của tôi không có nhiều thịt gà. Món tráng miệng, chúng tôi ăn chung một chiếc bánh xoài ngọt. Hóa đơn chỉ có hai mươi đô la. Tôi sẽ quay lại vào tháng sau cùng gia đình.

q: Vì sao họ không phải chờ bàn?
Why didn't they wait for a table?
e: “I booked a table for two, so we didn't wait.” – “so” nối nguyên nhân với kết quả.
“I booked a table for two, so we didn't wait.” – “so” links the cause and the result.
f: I booked a table for two

q: Người viết không hài lòng về điều gì?
What was the writer not happy about?
o: There wasn't much chicken in the rice.
e: “The food was delicious, but there wasn't much chicken in my rice.” Phục vụ thân thiện và hóa đơn “only twenty dollars”.
“The food was delicious, but there wasn't much chicken in my rice.” The waiter was friendly and the bill was “only twenty dollars”.

q: Món tráng miệng là gì?
What did they have for dessert?
e: “For dessert we shared a sweet mango cake.” Phở và cơm rang là món chính.
“For dessert we shared a sweet mango cake.” Pho and fried rice were the main dishes.

ex2.s: Could I have ___ water, please? I'm really thirsty after the long walk. (một ít)
a: some
e: Lời yêu cầu/mời dùng “some” dù là câu hỏi. “water” không đếm được nên không dùng “a”.
Requests and offers use “some”, even as questions. “water” is uncountable, so no “a”.

ex2.s: How ___ sugar do you want in your coffee – one spoon or two?
a: much
e: “sugar” không đếm được → How much. “How many” dùng với danh từ đếm được số nhiều (How many eggs?).
“sugar” is uncountable → How much. “How many” is for plural countable nouns (How many eggs?).

ex2.s: I'd ___ the chicken, please, and my friend would like the fish soup.
a: like
e: “I'd like” = I would like, cách gọi món lịch sự. Không dùng “I'd want”.
“I'd like” = I would like, the polite way to order. Don't say “I'd want”.

ex2.s: There aren't ___ tables free tonight, so we can't give you a table until nine o'clock.
e: Câu phủ định với danh từ đếm được số nhiều → “any”. “much” chỉ đi với danh từ không đếm được.
Negative sentence + plural countable noun → “any”. “much” only goes with uncountable nouns.

ex2.s: We didn't order much dishes because the portions in this restaurant are very big.
a: We didn't order many dishes because the portions in this restaurant are very big.
e: “dishes” là danh từ đếm được số nhiều → “many”, không phải “much”.
“dishes” is a plural countable noun → “many”, not “much”.

ex2.s: Tôi không ăn được đồ cay.
a: I can't eat spicy food.
I cannot eat spicy food.
I can't eat spicy things.
e: “không ăn được” = can't eat. “spicy” là tính từ đứng trước “food”.
“không ăn được” = can't eat. “spicy” is an adjective before “food”.

ex2.s: Cho tôi thêm một chai nước.
a: Could I have another bottle of water?
Could I have another bottle of water, please?
Can I have another bottle of water, please?
Could we have another bottle of water, please?
e: “thêm một” = another (an + other, viết liền). Danh từ không đếm được “water” cần đơn vị “a bottle of”.
“thêm một” = another (one word). Uncountable “water” needs a unit: “a bottle of”.

q: Viết lại cho lịch sự hơn, bắt đầu bằng “I'd like …”.
Make it more polite, starting with “I'd like …”.
ex2.s: I want a glass of orange juice and a plate of fried noodles with vegetables.
a: I'd like a glass of orange juice and a plate of fried noodles with vegetables.
I'd like a glass of orange juice and a plate of fried noodles with vegetables, please.
I would like a glass of orange juice and a plate of fried noodles with vegetables, please.
e: “I want” nghe thô khi gọi món; “I'd like” lịch sự hơn. Có thể thêm “please” ở cuối.
“I want” sounds rude when ordering; “I'd like” is polite. You can add “please” at the end.

ex2.s: Excuse me,|could we|have|some more|rice|and|two cups of|green tea,|please?
m: Xin lỗi, cho chúng tôi thêm ít cơm và hai tách trà xanh nhé?
Excuse me, could we have some more rice and two cups of green tea, please?
e: “some more rice” (rice không đếm được) nhưng “two cups of green tea” (đếm bằng cốc).
“some more rice” (uncountable) but “two cups of green tea” (counted in cups).

q: Viết công thức khoảng 100 từ một món Việt Nam bạn thích: danh sách nguyên liệu và 5 bước nấu, dùng câu mệnh lệnh.
Write a recipe of about 100 words for a Vietnamese dish you like: a list of ingredients and 5 steps, using imperatives.
ex2.m:
Vietnamese fried rice (for two people)
Ingredients: two bowls of cooked rice, two eggs, some chicken, one carrot, some green onions, a little fish sauce and some oil.
1. Cut the chicken and the carrot into small pieces.
2. Heat some oil in a pan and fry the chicken for five minutes.
3. Add the carrot and cook for two more minutes.
4. Put the rice and the eggs in the pan and mix everything well.
5. Add a little fish sauce and the green onions, then serve it hot.
It is quick, cheap and delicious!
e: Cần có: • danh sách nguyên liệu với some / a little / số lượng • 5 bước dùng câu mệnh lệnh (Cut, Fry, Add…) • từ nối thứ tự (then, after that) • đúng đếm được / không đếm được.
Include: • an ingredient list with some / a little / numbers • 5 imperative steps (Cut, Fry, Add…) • sequence words (then, after that) • correct countable / uncountable use.

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – so sánh hơn:** tính từ ngắn + **-er + than** (cheap → cheaper than, big → bigger than, easy → easier than); tính từ dài **more + adj + than** (more expensive than). Bất quy tắc: good → better, bad → worse.
• This jacket is cheaper than that one.
• The blue shoes are more expensive than the black ones.
• Online prices are often better than shop prices.

**Grammar 1 – comparatives:** short adjectives + **-er + than** (cheap → cheaper than, big → bigger than, easy → easier than); long adjectives **more + adj + than** (more expensive than). Irregular: good → better, bad → worse.
• This jacket is cheaper than that one.
• The blue shoes are more expensive than the black ones.
• Online prices are often better than shop prices.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – this / that / these / those:** this (số ít, gần), that (số ít, xa), these (số nhiều, gần), those (số nhiều, xa). Động từ phải hợp: **How much is this?** – **How much are these shoes?**
• Can I try on those jeans?
• That bag is too big for me.

**Grammar 2 – this / that / these / those:** this (singular, near), that (singular, far), these (plural, near), those (plural, far). The verb must agree: **How much is this?** – **How much are these shoes?**
• Can I try on those jeans?
• That bag is too big for me.

**Phát âm – thirteen hay thirty?** Số -teen nhấn âm cuối và có /n/: thir**TEEN** /θɝːˈtiːn/, fif**TEEN** /fɪfˈtiːn/. Số -ty nhấn âm đầu: **THIR**ty /ˈθɝː.t̬i/, **FIF**ty /ˈfɪf.ti/. Nghe sai là trả sai tiền!

**Pronunciation – thirteen or thirty?** -teen numbers stress the end and finish with /n/: thir**TEEN** /θɝːˈtiːn/, fif**TEEN** /fɪfˈtiːn/. -ty numbers stress the start: **THIR**ty /ˈθɝː.t̬i/, **FIF**ty /ˈfɪf.ti/. Mishear it and you pay the wrong price!

**Tự luyện ngoài app:**
• Nghe (20 phút): nghe 5 đoạn mua bán ngắn, ghi lại đúng con số giá tiền.
• Nói (20 phút): đóng vai mua 1 món quần áo – hỏi giá, hỏi cỡ, mặc cả, trả tiền.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 1 trang sản phẩm trên web bán hàng, tìm giá, chính sách đổi trả, phí giao hàng.
• Viết (30 phút): viết email 80 từ yêu cầu đổi hàng vì sai cỡ.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): đọc to 20 giá tiền ngẫu nhiên (15.99; 230; 1,450).
• Thử thách (20 phút): chọn 5 món trên một trang mua sắm tiếng Anh trong ngân sách cố định, đọc to tổng tiền.

**Practice outside the app:**
• Listening (20 min): listen to 5 short shopping dialogues and write down the exact prices.
• Speaking (20 min): role-play buying clothes – ask the price and size, bargain, pay.
• Reading (20 min): read a product page on a shopping site; find the price, return policy and delivery fee.
• Writing (30 min): write an 80-word email asking to exchange an item in the wrong size.
• Vocabulary (15 min): read 20 random prices aloud (15.99; 230; 1,450).
• Challenge (20 min): choose 5 items on an English shopping site within a fixed budget and say the total aloud.

warm.s: These trainers were fifty dollars last week, but today there's a discount, so they're only thirty-five.
q: Hôm nay đôi giày giá bao nhiêu?
How much are the trainers today?
e: “today … they're only thirty-five”. 50 là giá tuần trước. Chú ý “fifty” nhấn âm đầu, “fifteen” nhấn âm cuối.
“today … they're only thirty-five”. 50 was last week's price. Note “fifty” is stressed at the start, “fifteen” at the end.

warm.s: How much is this?
e: Hỏi giá một món: How much is this? Nhiều món: How much are these?
For one item: How much is this? For several: How much are these?

warm.s: Do you have it in a bigger size?
e: “big” → “bigger” (gấp đôi g). “in a … size” là cụm cố định.
“big” → “bigger” (double g). “in a … size” is a fixed phrase.

warm.s: Can you give me a discount?
e: “give me a discount” = bớt giá cho tôi. “discount” nhấn âm đầu /ˈdɪs.kaʊnt/.
“give me a discount” = lower the price for me. “discount” is stressed at the start /ˈdɪs.kaʊnt/.

warm.s: Can I pay by card?
e: Dùng “by card”, “in cash” – không có mạo từ.
Say “by card” and “in cash” – no article.

warm.s: I prefer shopping online because it's cheaper and faster, but I buy shoes in stores because I need to try them on.
e: Câu hỏi: Do you prefer shopping online or in stores? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Nhấn “cheaper”, “faster”; “try them on” đọc nối /ˈtraɪ ðəm ˈɑːn/.
Question: Do you prefer shopping online or in stores? – Model answer. Stress “cheaper” and “faster”; link “try them on” /ˈtraɪ ðəm ˈɑːn/.

rd2.tx:
Dear Customer Service,
Last week I bought a pair of jeans from your website. The price was forty dollars and I paid by card. Unfortunately, they are too small for me. I usually wear a size 30, but these jeans are smaller than my other size 30 jeans. I would like to return them and get a bigger size, a 32. I don't want my money back. Your website says that returns are free if the item is not worn. Could you tell me how to send them back? Also, is the size 32 more expensive than the size 30?
Thank you,
Linh Tran
rd2.tr:
Kính gửi bộ phận Chăm sóc khách hàng,
Tuần trước tôi đã mua một chiếc quần jeans trên trang web của quý công ty. Giá là bốn mươi đô la và tôi đã thanh toán bằng thẻ. Thật không may, chiếc quần quá nhỏ đối với tôi. Tôi thường mặc cỡ 30, nhưng chiếc quần này nhỏ hơn những chiếc quần cỡ 30 khác của tôi. Tôi muốn trả lại và đổi lấy cỡ lớn hơn, cỡ 32. Tôi không muốn lấy lại tiền. Trang web của quý công ty ghi rằng đổi trả miễn phí nếu sản phẩm chưa mặc. Quý công ty có thể cho tôi biết cách gửi trả không? Ngoài ra, cỡ 32 có đắt hơn cỡ 30 không?
Cảm ơn,
Trần Linh

q: Linh đã trả tiền bằng cách nào?
How did Linh pay?
e: “The price was forty dollars and I paid by card.”
“The price was forty dollars and I paid by card.”

q: Linh muốn gì?
What does Linh want?
e: “I would like to return them and get a bigger size” và cô ấy nói rõ “I don't want my money back”.
“I would like to return them and get a bigger size”, and she says “I don't want my money back”.

q: Theo trang web, khi nào đổi trả miễn phí?
According to the website, when are returns free?
o: When the item is not worn
When the price is under forty dollars
e: “returns are free if the item is not worn” – “worn” là quá khứ phân từ của wear (mặc).
“returns are free if the item is not worn” – “worn” is the past participle of wear.
f: if the item is not worn

ex2.s: This jacket is ___ than that one, but I think the quality is not as good. (cheap)
a: cheaper
e: Tính từ ngắn “cheap” → “cheaper than”. Không nói “more cheap”.
Short adjective “cheap” → “cheaper than”. Don't say “more cheap”.

ex2.s: How much ___ these shoes? They look really comfortable for walking.
a: are
e: “these shoes” là số nhiều → How much are. Lỗi hay gặp: “How much is these shoes”.
“these shoes” is plural → How much are. A common mistake is “How much is these shoes”.

ex2.s: Can I pay ___ card, or do you only accept cash in this small shop?
a: by
e: “pay by card” – giới từ “by”, không có “a/the”. Tiền mặt nói “in cash”.
“pay by card” – use “by” with no article. For cash, say “in cash”.

ex2.s: The red dress is nice, but the green one is ___ and it only costs twenty dollars.
e: So sánh hai món → so sánh hơn “cheaper”. “more cheap” sai; “cheapest” là so sánh nhất.
Comparing two items → comparative “cheaper”. “more cheap” is wrong; “cheapest” is superlative.

ex2.s: This laptop is more cheaper than the one in the shop next door, so I'm going to buy it.
a: This laptop is cheaper than the one in the shop next door, so I'm going to buy it.
e: Không dùng “more” cùng đuôi “-er”: chỉ cần “cheaper”.
Don't use “more” with “-er”: just “cheaper”.

ex2.s: Can I try on this jeans in a bigger size before I decide to buy them?
a: Can I try on these jeans in a bigger size before I decide to buy them?
Can I try these jeans on in a bigger size before I decide to buy them?
e: “jeans” luôn ở số nhiều → “these jeans”, không phải “this jeans”.
“jeans” is always plural → “these jeans”, not “this jeans”.

ex2.s: Cái áo này có màu khác không?
a: Do you have this shirt in another colour?
Do you have this shirt in another color?
Have you got this shirt in another colour?
Does this shirt come in another colour?
e: “có màu khác” = in another colour (Anh-Mỹ: color). Hỏi người bán: Do you have …?
“có màu khác” = in another colour (US: color). Ask the seller: Do you have …?

ex2.s: Tôi chỉ xem thôi, cảm ơn.
a: I'm just looking, thanks.
I'm just looking, thank you.
I am just looking, thanks.
e: Câu cố định khi người bán hỏi “Can I help you?”. Dùng hiện tại tiếp diễn “I'm just looking”.
Fixed reply when a seller asks “Can I help you?”. Use the present continuous “I'm just looking”.

ex2.s: Đôi giày màu đen đắt hơn đôi màu trắng, nhưng chúng thoải mái hơn nhiều.
a: The black shoes are more expensive than the white ones, but they are much more comfortable.
The black shoes are more expensive than the white ones, but they're much more comfortable.
The black shoes are more expensive than the white shoes, but they are much more comfortable.
e: Tính từ dài → more expensive, more comfortable. “nhiều” trước so sánh hơn = much. “ones” thay cho “shoes”.
Long adjectives → more expensive, more comfortable. Use “much” to make a comparative stronger. “ones” replaces “shoes”.

ex2.s: Excuse me,|do you|have|this jacket|in a smaller size?|It's|too big|for me.
m: Xin lỗi, chị có chiếc áo khoác này cỡ nhỏ hơn không? Nó quá rộng so với tôi.
Excuse me, do you have this jacket in a smaller size? It's too big for me.
e: “in a smaller size” đi sau tên món đồ; “too big for me” = quá to so với tôi.
“in a smaller size” comes after the item; “too big for me” = bigger than I need.

q: Viết đánh giá khoảng 100 từ về một món đồ bạn mới mua: giá, chất lượng, so với sản phẩm khác, có nên mua không.
Write a review of about 100 words of something you bought recently: price, quality, comparison with other products, and whether people should buy it.
ex2.m: Last month I bought a pair of running shoes online. They cost sixty dollars, but there was a twenty percent discount, so I only paid forty-eight. The quality is very good: they are lighter than my old shoes and much more comfortable. My friend has a famous brand that is more expensive than mine, but I think my shoes are better for long runs. The only problem is the colour – it is darker than in the photo. Should you buy them? Yes, if you want good shoes at a fair price.
e: Cần có: • giá và cách trả tiền • ít nhất 3 câu so sánh hơn (cheaper, lighter, more comfortable…) • một điểm chưa tốt • lời khuyên nên mua hay không.
Include: • the price and how you paid • at least 3 comparatives (cheaper, lighter, more comfortable…) • one weak point • a clear buy / don't buy recommendation.

t: Du lịch, phương tiện & chỉ đường
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – giới từ chỉ vị trí:** **next to** (bên cạnh), **opposite** (đối diện), **between … and …** (giữa), **on the corner of** (ở góc), **in front of** (phía trước), **behind** (phía sau).
• The bank is next to the post office.
• The hotel is opposite the train station.
• The café is between the bookshop and the pharmacy.

**Grammar 1 – prepositions of place:** **next to**, **opposite**, **between … and …**, **on the corner of**, **in front of**, **behind**.
• The bank is next to the post office.
• The hotel is opposite the train station.
• The café is between the bookshop and the pharmacy.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – câu mệnh lệnh & be going to:** chỉ đường bằng động từ nguyên mẫu đứng đầu câu: **Go straight on. Turn left at the traffic lights. Take the second road on the right.** Kế hoạch đã quyết định dùng **be going to + V**.
• Go straight on, then turn left.
• We're going to visit Da Lat next month.

**Grammar 2 – imperatives & be going to:** give directions with the base verb at the start: **Go straight on. Turn left at the traffic lights. Take the second road on the right.** For decided plans use **be going to + verb**.
• Go straight on, then turn left.
• We're going to visit Da Lat next month.

**Ngữ pháp 1 – there is / there are + some / any**
• Số ít: **There is** a balcony. **There isn't** a dishwasher.
• Số nhiều: **There are** two bedrooms. **There aren't any** shelves in the kitchen.
• Câu hỏi: **Is there** a lift? **Are there any** shops nearby? – Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
• Giới từ nơi chốn: next to, opposite, near, between, on the fifth floor.

**Grammar 1 – there is / there are + some / any**
• Singular: **There is** a balcony. **There isn't** a dishwasher.
• Plural: **There are** two bedrooms. **There aren't any** shelves in the kitchen.
• Questions: **Is there** a lift? **Are there any** shops nearby? – Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
• Prepositions of place: next to, opposite, near, between, on the fifth floor.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – so sánh khi chọn nhà**
• Tính từ ngắn: cheap → **cheaper than**, big → **bigger than**, quiet → **quieter than**.
• Tính từ dài: **more modern than**, **more expensive than**.
• Bất quy tắc: good → better, bad → worse, far → further.
• Ví dụ: The flat in District 3 is smaller, but it's cheaper and closer to my office.

**Grammar 2 – comparing places to live**
• Short adjectives: cheap → **cheaper than**, big → **bigger than**, quiet → **quieter than**.
• Long adjectives: **more modern than**, **more expensive than**.
• Irregular: good → better, bad → worse, far → further.
• Example: The flat in District 3 is smaller, but it's cheaper and closer to my office.

**Phát âm – trọng âm danh từ ghép**
• Danh từ ghép thường nhấn từ **đầu**: **LIV**ing room, **BED**room, **BATH**room, **WASH**ing machine, **BUS** stop.
• Từ cần chú ý: furnished /ˈfɝː.nɪʃt/ (đuôi -ed đọc /t/), deposit /dɪˈpɑː.zɪt/, landlord /ˈlænd.lɔːrd/.

**Pronunciation – stress in compound nouns**
• Compound nouns are usually stressed on the **first** part: **LIV**ing room, **BED**room, **BATH**room, **WASH**ing machine, **BUS** stop.
• Watch out: furnished /ˈfɝː.nɪʃt/ (-ed = /t/), deposit /dɪˈpɑː.zɪt/, landlord /ˈlænd.lɔːrd/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): xem 1 video house tour bằng tiếng Anh, ghi lại các phòng và 5 đồ vật.
• Nói (15 phút): mô tả nhà/phòng bạn đang ở trong 1 phút với there is/there are và giới từ.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 3 tin cho thuê nhà bằng tiếng Anh, so sánh giá, diện tích, tiện ích.

• Từ vựng (10 phút): học 15 từ: landlord, tenant, rent, deposit, bills, furnished, balcony, lift, wardrobe, sofa, fridge, microwave, washing machine, neighbour, lease.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): watch an English house-tour video; note the rooms and 5 objects.
• Speaking (15 min): describe your home or room for 1 minute with there is/there are and prepositions.
• Reading (20 min): read 3 English rental ads; compare price, size and facilities.
• Writing (20 min): write a 60–80-word message to a landlord asking about a flat (price, deposit, pets, viewing date).
• Vocabulary (10 min): learn 15 words: landlord, tenant, rent, deposit, bills, furnished, balcony, lift, wardrobe, sofa, fridge, microwave, washing machine, neighbour, lease.

ex2.s: Tôi đang tìm một căn hộ nhỏ gần trường đại học, có máy giặt và không quá đắt.

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – play / go / do + môn thể thao**
• **play** + môn có bóng, đối kháng: play football, play badminton, play tennis.
• **go** + môn đuôi -ing: go swimming, go running, go cycling, go jogging.
• **do** + môn cá nhân, không bóng: do yoga, do karate, do exercise, do aerobics.
• Ví dụ: I play badminton on Mondays and go swimming at the weekend. My mum does yoga every morning.

**Grammar 1 – play / go / do + sport**
• **play** + ball games and competitive games: play football, play badminton, play tennis.
• **go** + activities ending in -ing: go swimming, go running, go cycling, go jogging.
• **do** + individual activities without a ball: do yoga, do karate, do exercise, do aerobics.
• Example: I play badminton on Mondays and go swimming at the weekend. My mum does yoga every morning.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – quá khứ đơn & lời khuyên với should**
• Kể buổi tập/trận đấu: I **ran** 5 km. We **won** 2–1. I **didn't stop** once.
• Bất quy tắc thường gặp: run → ran, swim → swam, win → won, lose → lost, take part → took part.
• Lời khuyên: You **should** warm up before running. You **shouldn't** exercise right after a big meal.

**Grammar 2 – past simple & advice with should**
• Describing a training session or match: I **ran** 5 km. We **won** 2–1. I **didn't stop** once.
• Common irregular verbs: run → ran, swim → swam, win → won, lose → lost, take part → took part.
• Advice: You **should** warm up before running. You **shouldn't** exercise right after a big meal.

**Phát âm – đuôi -ed**
• /t/ sau âm vô thanh: stretched /stretʃt/, jumped /dʒʌmpt/, walked /wɔːkt/.
• /d/ sau âm hữu thanh: trained /treɪnd/, joined /dʒɔɪnd/, played /pleɪd/.
• /ɪd/ sau t, d: started /ˈstɑːr.t̬ɪd/, needed /ˈniː.dɪd/.
• Đừng thêm âm /ɪd/ vào mọi động từ: “walked” không đọc là “walk-ed”.

**Pronunciation – -ed endings**
• /t/ after voiceless sounds: stretched /stretʃt/, jumped /dʒʌmpt/, walked /wɔːkt/.
• /d/ after voiced sounds: trained /treɪnd/, joined /dʒɔɪnd/, played /pleɪd/.
• /ɪd/ after t and d: started /ˈstɑːr.t̬ɪd/, needed /ˈniː.dɪd/.
• Don't add /ɪd/ to every verb: “walked” is not “walk-ed”.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): nghe/xem bình luận 5 phút một trận đấu, ghi tỉ số và 5 động từ quá khứ.
• Nói (15 phút): kể buổi tập gần nhất trong 1 phút (where, how long, how you felt), chú ý đuôi -ed.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 1 bài “10 tips for beginner runners”, chọn 3 lời khuyên với should.
• Viết (20 phút): viết nhật ký tập luyện 1 tuần (5–7 câu, quá khứ đơn).
• Từ vựng (10 phút): học 15 từ: warm up, stretch, coach, team, match, score, win, lose, draw, gym, training, race, injury, fit, muscles.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): listen to 5 minutes of match commentary; note the score and 5 past-tense verbs.
• Speaking (15 min): describe your last workout in 1 minute (where, how long, how you felt); watch the -ed endings.
• Reading (20 min): read a “10 tips for beginner runners” article; choose 3 pieces of advice with should.
• Writing (20 min): keep a one-week training diary (5–7 sentences in the past simple).
• Vocabulary (10 min): learn 15 words: warm up, stretch, coach, team, match, score, win, lose, draw, gym, training, race, injury, fit, muscles.

t: Gọi điện, hẹn lịch & lời mời
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – hiện tại tiếp diễn cho lịch hẹn tương lai**
• Việc đã sắp xếp, có giờ, có người: I'**m meeting** Lan at 7 tonight. We'**re flying** to Hue on Friday.
• Dùng để từ chối lời mời một cách tự nhiên: Sorry, I'**m working** on Saturday.
• Hỏi lịch: **Are you doing** anything on Sunday? / **Are you free** on Thursday?

**Grammar 1 – present continuous for future arrangements**
• Fixed plans with a time and other people: I'**m meeting** Lan at 7 tonight. We'**re flying** to Hue on Friday.
• A natural way to decline: Sorry, I'**m working** on Saturday.
• Asking about plans: **Are you doing** anything on Sunday? / **Are you free** on Thursday?

**Ngữ pháp 2 – mời, gợi ý, nhận lời, từ chối**
• Mời: **Would you like to** come to my party? (to + V)
• Gợi ý: **How about** + V-ing? (How about having lunch?) / **Let's** + V / **Shall we** + V?
• Nhận lời: I'd love to! / Sounds good! / That's a great idea.
• Từ chối lịch sự: I'd love to, **but** I'm busy. / I'm afraid I can't make it.
• Gọi điện: Could I speak to …? / I'd like to make an appointment. / Can I leave a message?

**Grammar 2 – inviting, suggesting, accepting, declining**
• Invite: **Would you like to** come to my party? (to + verb)
• Suggest: **How about** + -ing? (How about having lunch?) / **Let's** + verb / **Shall we** + verb?
• Accept: I'd love to! / Sounds good! / That's a great idea.
• Decline politely: I'd love to, **but** I'm busy. / I'm afraid I can't make it.
• On the phone: Could I speak to …? / I'd like to make an appointment. / Can I leave a message?

**Phát âm – đọc số điện thoại & giờ**
• Đọc từng số; số 0 thường đọc **“oh”** /oʊ/; hai số giống nhau có thể đọc **“double”**: 554 = double five four.
• Ngắt nhóm 3–4 số, lên giọng cuối mỗi nhóm, xuống giọng ở nhóm cuối.
• Giờ: 3:30 = half past three / three thirty; 7:15 = a quarter past seven.

**Pronunciation – phone numbers & times**
• Say each digit; 0 is often **“oh”** /oʊ/; two same digits can be **“double”**: 554 = double five four.
• Pause between groups of 3–4 digits, rising at the end of each group and falling on the last one.
• Times: 3:30 = half past three / three thirty; 7:15 = a quarter past seven.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): nghe 3 đoạn hội thoại điện thoại mẫu (đặt lịch, để lại lời nhắn), ghi tên, ngày, giờ, số điện thoại.
• Nói (15 phút): tự đọc to 5 số điện thoại và 5 giờ hẹn; đóng vai gọi đặt lịch cắt tóc.
• Đọc (15 phút): đọc 5 tin nhắn mời/từ chối, đánh dấu cụm nhận lời và từ chối.
• Viết (20 phút): viết 2 tin nhắn 40–60 từ: mời bạn đi ăn sinh nhật và từ chối lịch sự một lời mời.
• Từ vựng (10 phút): học 12 cụm: make/cancel/change an appointment, call back, hang up, leave a message, be free, be busy, invite, accept, decline, reschedule.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): listen to 3 sample phone calls (booking, leaving a message); note names, days, times, numbers.
• Speaking (15 min): read aloud 5 phone numbers and 5 appointment times; role-play booking a haircut.
• Reading (15 min): read 5 invitation/refusal messages; mark the phrases for accepting and declining.
• Writing (20 min): write 2 messages of 40–60 words: inviting a friend to a birthday dinner and politely declining an invitation.
• Vocabulary (10 min): learn 12 phrases: make/cancel/change an appointment, call back, hang up, leave a message, be free, be busy, invite, accept, decline, reschedule.

**Ngữ pháp 1 – câu mệnh lệnh và từ nối trình tự**
• Công thức dùng câu mệnh lệnh (động từ nguyên mẫu ở đầu câu): **Chop** the onion. **Heat** the oil. **Don't** add too much salt.
• Từ nối: **First**, … **Then** … **After that**, … **When** the water boils, … **Finally**, …
• Ví dụ: First, wash the rice. Then put it in the pot with two cups of water. Finally, cook it for 20 minutes.

**Grammar 1 – imperatives and sequencers**
• Recipes use imperatives (base verb at the start): **Chop** the onion. **Heat** the oil. **Don't** add too much salt.
• Sequencers: **First**, … **Then** … **After that**, … **When** the water boils, … **Finally**, …
• Example: First, wash the rice. Then put it in the pot with two cups of water. Finally, cook it for 20 minutes.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – danh từ đếm được / không đếm được**
• Đếm được: an egg, two onions, **a few** tomatoes, **How many** eggs?
• Không đếm được: rice, oil, salt, sugar, water → **a little** oil, **some** salt, **How much** sugar?
• Đơn vị đo cho danh từ không đếm được: a cup **of** rice, a spoon **of** sugar, a pinch **of** salt, a bottle **of** fish sauce.
• Lỗi hay gặp: “two rices”, “many salt” ✗.

**Grammar 2 – countable and uncountable nouns**
• Countable: an egg, two onions, **a few** tomatoes, **How many** eggs?
• Uncountable: rice, oil, salt, sugar, water → **a little** oil, **some** salt, **How much** sugar?
• Containers/measures for uncountable nouns: a cup **of** rice, a spoon **of** sugar, a pinch **of** salt, a bottle **of** fish sauce.
• Common mistakes: “two rices”, “many salt” ✗.

**Phát âm**
• Dạng yếu của “of” /əv/ và “a” /ə/: a cup of rice = /ə ˈkʌp əv raɪs/ – đọc nhanh, nối âm.
• Âm /ɔɪ/: boil, oil, soy – miệng tròn rồi kéo sang /ɪ/.
• Từ dễ đọc sai: recipe /ˈres.ə.pi/ (3 âm tiết), vegetable /ˈvedʒ.tə.bəl/ (3 âm tiết), sauce /sɑːs/.

**Pronunciation**
• Weak forms of “of” /əv/ and “a” /ə/: a cup of rice = /ə ˈkʌp əv raɪs/ – said quickly and linked.
• The /ɔɪ/ sound: boil, oil, soy – round lips, then glide to /ɪ/.
• Easy to mispronounce: recipe /ˈres.ə.pi/ (3 syllables), vegetable /ˈvedʒ.tə.bəl/ (3 syllables), sauce /sɑːs/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): xem 1 video nấu ăn ngắn bằng tiếng Anh, ghi lại nguyên liệu và 6 động từ nấu ăn.
• Nói (15 phút): vừa nấu một món đơn giản vừa nói to từng bước bằng tiếng Anh (First, … Then, …).
• Đọc (15 phút): đọc 2 công thức trên một trang nấu ăn tiếng Anh, gạch chân đơn vị đo.
• Viết (25 phút): viết công thức 80–100 từ cho một món Việt bạn biết nấu.
• Từ vựng (10 phút): học 15 từ: chop, slice, peel, boil, fry, stir, bake, mix, pour, add, pan, pot, oven, spoon, ingredients.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): watch a short English cooking video; note the ingredients and 6 cooking verbs.
• Speaking (15 min): cook a simple dish and say each step aloud in English (First, … Then, …).
• Reading (15 min): read 2 recipes on an English cooking website; underline the measurements.
• Writing (25 min): write an 80–100-word recipe for a Vietnamese dish you can cook.
• Vocabulary (10 min): learn 15 words: chop, slice, peel, boil, fry, stir, bake, mix, pour, add, pan, pot, oven, spoon, ingredients.

Easy egg fried rice (for two people)
You need: two cups of cooked rice, two eggs, a small onion, some peas, a little oil, two spoons of soy sauce and some salt.
First, chop the onion. Then heat a little oil in a large pan. Fry the onion for two minutes until it is soft. After that, add the eggs and stir quickly. When the eggs are almost cooked, add the rice and the peas. Cook everything for five minutes and don't stop stirring. Finally, add the soy sauce and a pinch of salt. Serve it hot. Tip: cold rice from the day before is better than fresh rice, because it is drier.
